title: Make recoverable invariant violations visible in Vaporize tests and launched runs
createdBy: codex@loom from operator direction to use swift-issue-reporting and create a bead family around Vaporize visibility

historicalContent.operatorDirection: Use Point-Free swift-issue-reporting and create beads around making recoverable invariant visibility show up through Vaporize.
historicalContent.problem: Vaporize can compile a product and forward test process output, but it has no first-class runtime-issue event or receipt model. A compile-only build cannot execute reportIssue, tests expose unexpected reports only as framework failures, and app launch delegates to open without ingesting the Apple runtime-issue stream. The dependency and the runtime evidence therefore need separate, explicit adoption steps.
historicalContent.desiredState: Vaporize preserves IssueReporting's default developer experience while also collecting structured, redacted issue events for test and launched-run receipts. Build diagnostics remain a distinct category and no receipt claims that runtime invariants were exercised during compilation.
policy: Expected domain, user, network, and validation failures remain typed errors or operational recovery, not reported invariants.
A recoverable invariant report must name a deterministic containment action; reporting must not silently alter control flow.
Unsafe continuation remains a precondition or fatal boundary.
The default Xcode runtime warning and native test-failure behavior remain enabled when the Vaporize reporter is appended.
Production escalation is configured separately from development and test failure policy.
acceptanceCriteria: The Vaporize package resolves one IssueReporting module implementation at an exact accepted release line.
A severity and containment policy distinguishes expected errors, recoverable invariants, unsafe continuation, and external operational failures.
A Sendable custom reporter emits typed, redacted Vaporize issue events without replacing the default reporter.
Unexpected reports in tests fail the test and appear as structured evidence in the Vaporize test receipt.
A launched fixture app can emit a recoverable invariant that appears in a Vaporize run receipt with source location and request correlation.
Compile-only build receipts explicitly report runtimeIssueExecution as not-run rather than zero-proven.
The IRC state-machine pilot proves reporting plus deterministic containment at a real consumer seam.
outOfScope: Turning IssueReporting into CommonLog or a substrate-wide logging facade.
Treating every thrown error, failed command, or user input problem as an invariant violation.
Replacing fatal or precondition failures where continuation is unsafe.
Claiming a build exercised runtime code merely because IssueReporting compiled into the product.
